title: People Ops Handbook: Working at Redwood - Roles, Benefits, Hiring & Tools
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

This People Ops handbook provides a single-page reference for working at Redwood: culture and expectations, role and career ladder summaries, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding workflow, and how to get access to core internal tools. This page is intended for new hires, hiring managers, and cross-functional partners who support hiring and onboarding.

1) Working at Redwood

Summary
- Mission-first: we prioritize shipping reliable inference features and making customers successful.
- Engineering-first culture: we value clear APIs, observability, and pragmatic tradeoffs that improve production reliability.
- High-trust distributed team: hybrid-remote by design with synchronous overlap expectations.

Core working norms
- Core hours: teams typically maintain a 10:00-16:00 local overlap window for meetings.
- Meeting etiquette: agenda required for >30m meetings; meeting notes captured on Confluence and assigned action owners.
- Async-first: use documented RFCs/ADR for major design decisions and prefer documented discussions on Confluence/Slack threads.
- Communication: Slack for fast operational signals, Confluence for long-form decisions, and GitHub for code review and PR discussions.

Hybrid & remote policy highlights
- Team-level flexibility: managers define office cadence for collaboration-heavy activities; people-ops recommends 1-2 onsite weeks per quarter for cross-team alignment.
- Travel & expenses: approved onsite travel is reimbursable per finance policy (see /confluence/finance-and-legal/expense-policy).

2) Roles & Career Ladders

Purpose
- Provide clear expectations for progression, promotion cycles, and manager/IC role differentiation. Ladders exist for Engineering, Product, Research/Applied ML, Design, People Ops, Sales/Go-to-Market, and Support.

Level summary (example for Engineering)
- IC1 (New Grad / Associate Engineer) - learns codebase, completes scoped tasks, requires coaching.
- IC2 (Software Engineer) - delivers features independently, owns small services or components.
- IC3 (Senior Software Engineer) - drives project-level technical ownership, mentors others.
- IC4 (Staff Engineer) - cross-team technical leadership, shapes architecture and operational standards.
- IC5 (Principal Engineer) - broad technical strategy, leads multiple initiative areas.
- EM1-EM3 (Engineering Manager levels) - Manager expectations scale from team execution to multi-team service ownership and org-level strategy.

Progression & promotion process
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet (impact examples, metrics, PR links) and shares with manager.
2. Manager compiles feedback from peers, direct reports, and cross-functional partners.
3. Calibration panel reviews packet against leveling rubric and gives recommendation.
4. HR/People Ops records decision, communicates outcome, and updates career ladder records.

Promotion criteria (high-level)
- Impact: measurable outcomes tied to product/operational metrics.
- Scope: number of teams, systems, or product areas influenced.
- Leadership: mentoring, design reviews, and cross-functional influence.
- Craft: technical depth, ownership, and code quality.

Ownership & resources
- Leveling rubric, manager guide, and promotion packet templates: /confluence/company-handbook/leveling-and-promotion-rubric (referenced).

3) Benefits & Perks

Introduction
Redwood offers a competitive benefits package designed to support total well-being, career development, and family needs. Below is a summary and quick reference for eligibility. For full plan documents and vendor contracts see Finance & Legal benefits pages.

Benefits summary table
Benefit | Eligibility | Notes
--- | --- | ---
Medical / Dental / Vision | All full-time employees (FTE) | Company covers ~85% of premium for employee; dependents optional enrollment during new hire or open enrollment
401(k) with match | All FTE | 401(k) match up to 4% after 1 month of employment; vesting per plan document
Equity (RSUs / Options) | All hires (level-dependent) | Grant schedule in offer letter; refresh guidance in compensation docs
Parental leave | FTE, 90 days tenure recommended | Primary/secondary parental leave policies; return-to-work flexibility
Paid Time Off (PTO) | All FTE | Flexible PTO policy; minimum 15 days/year recommended; submit in Workday
Learning & development stipend | Full-time employees | $1,500/year L&D stipend, discretionary approval for conferences/courses
Home office & relocation stipend | New hires (role-dependent) | One-time home office stipend ($800) and relocation reimbursement when approved
Commuter/transport benefits | US-based employees | Pre-tax options or monthly commuter allowance where applicable
Wellness & mental health | All FTE | Therapy sessions covered via EAP; Headspace/mental health app stipend available

How to enroll / important contacts
- Enrollment: new hires enroll in Workday within first 30 days. Benefits questions: benefits@redwood-inference.com.
- Benefits coordinator: Priya Menon (people-ops).

4) Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Hiring pipeline overview (high level)
1. Requisition created and approved by hiring manager + finance.
2. Recruiter builds interview loop and scorecard aligned to role rubric.
3. Candidate interviews: typically 3-5 rounds (screen, technical, onsite/loop, hiring manager).
4. Hiring committee review for IC4+ or as required by role.
5. Offer issued, background check, and reference checks as needed.

Typical timelines
- Standard roles: 2-4 weeks from first screen to offer (depends on availability).
- Senior / executive: 4-8+ weeks, includes hiring committee and extra stakeholder interviews.

New hire checklist (quick)
- Before day 1: offer accepted, recruit sends welcome packet, IT begins account provisioning.
- Day 1: orientation (people-ops), manager 1:1, team intro, Slack/GitHub/Confluence access confirmed.
- Week 1: environment setup, project onboarding, buddy assigned, first small deliverable.
- Month 1: 30-day check-in (manager + people-ops), training milestones.
- 60/90-day: career conversation and performance alignment.

90-day onboarding plan (example)
Week 0 (pre-start): paperwork, equipment shipped, account access pre-provisioned.
Week 1: meet the team, complete mandatory training (security, compliance, codebase overview).
Weeks 2-4: shadowing, first PRs, ownership of an identified low-risk task.
Month 2: deeper system ownership, cross-team pairing.
Month 3: deliver a project milestone and participate in a roadmap planning cycle.

Manager & buddy responsibilities
- Manager: set clear 30/60/90 goals, schedule regular 1:1s, provide feedback and context.
- Buddy: day-to-day questions, context for team norms, and codebase pointers for the first 4-8 weeks.

5) Internal Tools & Access

Core systems (typical)
- Communication & docs: Slack, Confluence.
- Source control: GitHub (repo-level access controlled by CODEOWNERS and team membership).
- Issue tracking & planning: Jira.
- Observability & SRE: Datadog, Honeycomb, Sentry.
- Incident & on-call: PagerDuty, Statuspage.
- Cloud & infra: GCP console (via IAM groups), AWS (for some dedicated workflows).
- Identity & SSO: Okta (single sign-on).
- HR & payroll: Workday for time off and payroll self-service.

Access request process (standard)
1. New hires: recruiter/IT opens access ticket in ServiceNow with job code and manager approval.
2. Manager verifies required tool list and approves role-based access.
3. IT provisions accounts and confirms via Slack DM to new hire.
4. If elevated privileges are required (production, billing), manager files an exception request and security reviews.

Sample access request template (paste into ServiceNow ticket)
- New hire name: 
- Role & team: 
- Start date: 
- Required system access: Slack, Confluence, GitHub (team X), Jira, GCP-project Y 
- Elevated privileges required (yes/no): 
- Manager approval (email): 

Security & compliance note
- Production/secret access requires separate justification and is gated by security review. All access is logged and audited. See /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth for full process.

6) First 30/60/90 example checklists (for managers)

30-day objectives
- Ensure all accounts/provisioning complete.
- New hire has completed core trainings: security, data handling, code of conduct.
- New hire has shipped first small PR or documented code review feedback.

60-day objectives
- New hire owns part of a service or feature.
- Regular feedback loop established and career goals discussed.

90-day objectives
- New hire delivers a measurable outcome tied to product metric or operational stability.
- Manager provides calibration and confirms ongoing development plan.
